turnLimitScope: One ACP prompt; cancel/stop on any tool-call or client permission request. Top-level --max-turns is not forwarded to the agent branch in the inspected official source.
prompt:
Metadata-only design review; no tools/web/files. RealBud is a local business desktop. Its private journal retains at most 8 prior workflow-pack configurations for rollback. A deliberate user-reviewed archive operation should retain the newest rollback configurations and externalize older snapshots into private immutable content-addressed files. Do not change active configuration, approvals, schedules, business data, or retirement/ownership claims. Archive preview/confirmation must bind to exact generation, history and selection. Hashes verify exact bytes; archive must be durable before journal references change. Operations need crash recovery and exact retries. Private backup/restore must include archives and refuse missing/tampered referenced files. No automatic pruning, hidden data loss, live clients, or external calls.
Return the top 3 concrete design failure paths and tests for this archival operation. Focus on actual interleavings (stale confirmation, partial writes, crash/retry, cross-profile/wrong-pack substitution, backup races) and which durable state proves success. Explain any remaining integrity/authenticity limits of plain hashes. Rank by severity. Return JSON {"cases":[{"title":"...","setup":"...","assertions":["..."]}]} with exactly 3 cases, at most 4 assertions each, under 280 words. This is design advice, not implementation or test evidence.
authentication: Existing cached auth via opaque symlink in disposable private GROK_HOME; harness never opens auth contents.

cases.title: S1 stale or cross-profile commit
cases.setup: Confirm binds P, pack K, generation G, history H, and older selection S. Shift H, or replay the token on P2 or K2.
assertions: Mismatch of profile, pack, G, H, or S aborts; journal and active config stay unchanged.
Only S is removed from the journal; newest 8, active config, approvals, schedules, business data, and ownership or retirement claims unchanged.
Proof is the new journal plus private content-addressed bytes hashing to S, not a status flag.
A foreign profile or pack token cannot select or drop rows.

cases.title: S2 crash before durable ref swap
cases.setup: Kill after temp write, hash, or pre-fsync, and after ref edit but before journal fsync. Retry the same confirm once H has moved.
assertions: Refs update only after durable read-back equals confirmed bytes and hash.
Retry completes or no-ops that pair; it never prunes or follows a newer S.
No crash leaves a missing, short, or hash-mismatched ref.
Active config and unselected history stay byte-identical.

cases.title: S3 backup race and plain-hash limits
cases.setup: Backup overlaps archive and may store new refs without files, or files without the journal. Restore missing, short, re-digested, and cross-pack files.
assertions: Complete backup has the post-archive journal and every referenced byte; else it is incomplete. Bad restores fail closed, no prune.
Restored journal matches rollback and active config; archives are included, not only the live 8.
A plain hash only shows bytes match a digest. It does not bind profile, pack, generation, or confirmation; rewriting journal and file together forges a pair.
No external calls, live clients, or automatic deletes.
